title: Robots Influencing Humans to Reveal their Goals during Collaboration and Competition
abstract: arXiv:2609.05519v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We propose a unified strategy for fast goal inference in human-robot interaction. The core idea is to drive the human toward Critical Decision Points (CDPs)-states where competing human strategies prescribe different next actions and thus maximally reveal the goal. We formalise CDPs using a goal-conditioned policy divergence measure and incorporate them into a Receding-Horizon Planner that explores future action sequences while optimizing a cost function balancing task progress and information gain. We evaluate this approach in both a collaborative, fully observable cooking task and a competitive, partially observable hide-and-seek game, each in simulation and on real robots. In both scenarios, our method infers human goals more accurately and earlier than baseline strategies.

translated_title: 机器人在协作与竞争情境中影响人类以揭示其目标
translated_abstract: 我们提出了一种在人机交互中实现快速目标推断的统一策略。其核心思想是将人类引导至关键决策点（CDPs）——即在这些状态下，相互竞争的人类策略会规定不同的下一步动作，从而最大程度地揭示其目标。我们使用目标条件策略散度度量对CDPs进行形式化，并将其纳入滚动时域规划器中，该规划器在探索未来动作序列的同时，优化一个平衡任务进展与信息增益的代价函数。我们在协作式全可观测的烹饪任务和竞争式部分可观测的捉迷藏游戏中评估了该方法，两者均在仿真环境和真实机器人上进行了实验。在两种场景中，我们的方法都比基线策略更准确、更早地推断出人类目标。
tldr: 该论文提出通过主动将人类引导至关键决策点（CDPs）来加速人机交互中的目标推断，在协作烹饪和竞争捉迷藏任务的仿真与真实机器人实验中，均比基线方法更早、更准确地推断出人类目标。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a unified strategy that actively steers humans toward Critical Decision Points (CDPs) to accelerate goal inference in human-robot interaction, achieving earlier and more accurate goal inference than baseline methods in both collaborative cooking and competitive hide-and-seek tasks across simulation and real-robot experiments.
